title: Pelvic fracture and binder
stem: Resus 2. A 45-year-old woman was struck from the front by a reversing bus and pinned against a wall at hip level. She complains of severe pain in her hips. HR 136, BP 78/40, RR 26, SpO2 96% on oxygen, GCS 15. She arrives on a scoop with no pelvic binder. You lead the team.

phases.title: Prepare
phases.goal: Team, PPE, blood and the binder ready; monitoring on; the handover.

phases.title: Primary survey
phases.goal: Examine her yourself: is the pelvis the source? Handle it gently.

phases.title: Resuscitate
phases.goal: Access in the arms, blood, and the drugs from the cart.

phases.title: Adjuncts and definitive care
phases.goal: Bedside imaging; who stops the bleeding? Hand over.

events.say: She is paler and confused. BP 64/36.
events.untreated: She bled from her pelvis and no binder went on.

review.text: Contraindications to a binder. Your notes list open pelvic fractures and stable fractures. An open fracture still gets a binder if the patient is bleeding (pack the wound under it); a stable fracture simply does not need one. There is no absolute contraindication.

notes:
Checked against ATLS 11th edition (2025), NICE NG39 (major trauma), and the BOAST guideline on pelvic and acetabular fractures.

An anteroposterior compression injury (open book) springs the symphysis apart and tears the posterior sacroiliac ligaments; the pelvic volume increases and it bleeds mostly from the presacral venous plexus (about 85%), less often from arteries (internal iliac branches). A binder closes the ring and tamponades venous bleeding.

The binder goes over the greater trochanters, not the iliac crests. Bring the feet and knees together and tie them. Do not spring the pelvis to test it, and avoid unnecessary log rolls before the binder is on.

Your notes list open pelvic fractures and stable fractures as contraindications. ATLS and NICE advise a binder for suspected pelvic bleeding in shock, open fractures included (wound packing under it); stable fractures simply do not need one. Your notes are otherwise consistent: greater trochanters, no absolute contraindication, skin checks, radiolucent device.

Transient responders with pelvic bleeding go to angioembolisation, or pre-peritoneal packing with external fixation, depending on the centre. Non-responders do not go to CT. REBOA zone 3 is a bridge in some centres.

In a man, blood at the meatus, a high-riding prostate or scrotal haematoma means no blind urethral catheter until the urethra is imaged.

steps.label: Get the bay ready
steps.hint: Trauma call, PPE, blood and the major haemorrhage protocol, warmer, a pelvic binder.

opts.t: Trauma team call
PPE for the team
Activate the major haemorrhage protocol; O-negative to the bedside
opts.mark: Activates the major haemorrhage protocol early

opts.t: Commercial pelvic binder ready on the trolley
Warmer, rapid infuser, warm air blanket
Urinary catheter set to put in first
opts.r: Not before the urethra and perineum are checked, and it is not a priority in the primary survey.

steps.label: Monitoring
steps.hint: Ask the nurse to put the patient on the monitor.

opts.t: Put her on the monitor: ECG leads, NIBP cuff and SpO2 probe.
opts.mark: Asks for continuous ECG, NIBP and SpO2 monitoring

Mechanism.r: Bus reversing, crushed her against a wall at hip height for a few seconds. 30 minutes ago.
Mechanism.mark: Asks the mechanism: front-to-back compression of the pelvis

Injuries.r: Pain across both hips and the lower back. Can't move her legs because of the pain. No head injury.

Signs.r: At scene HR 110, BP 100/60. Now worse.
Signs.mark: Asks the trend of the vital signs

Treatment.r: Oxygen, one 16 G, 500 mL saline, 5 mg morphine. We didn't have a binder on the vehicle.

steps.label: Primary survey
steps.hint: xABCDE. Look at the pelvis and legs; do not spring it.

x A B.r: Equal air entry, no tenderness, RR 26.

Circulation.r: Weak radial pulse 136. Cold peripheries. CRT 5 s.
Soft. Suprapubic bruising, tender low down.

Circulation.t: Look at the pelvis and legs
Circulation.r: Both legs externally rotated, bruising over the symphysis and a labial haematoma. Leg lengths equal.
Circulation.mark: Looks for pelvic signs: rotation, bruising, perineal haematoma

Circulation.t: Press gently once over the iliac wings
Circulation.r: She cries out. You stop: a pelvic injury is assumed and a binder goes on.

Circulation.t: Spring the pelvis hard to test for instability
Circulation.r: Springing a disrupted pelvis dislodges clot and restarts the bleeding.

D E.t: Full log roll now to look at her back
D E.r: Every roll moves the fracture. Minimise log rolls until the pelvis is bound and imaged.

steps.label: Pelvic binder
steps.hint: Empty pockets, slide it under the knees and up to the greater trochanters, feet together, tighten, check.

opts.t: Explain to her; empty pockets and remove belts
opts.mark: Explains and clears pockets before applying

opts.t: Slide the binder under the knees and work it up to the hips without log rolling
opts.mark: Positions the binder with minimal movement

opts.t: Centre it over the greater trochanters
opts.mark: Binder centred on the greater trochanters

opts.t: Bring the feet and knees together and tie them
opts.mark: Internally rotates and ties the legs together

opts.t: Tighten until it locks; note the time on the binder
opts.r: It clicks. Nurse Chan writes 10:42 on the strap. Her pain eases.

opts.t: Recheck the pulse and pressure
Place it over the iliac crests
opts.r: Over the crests it can open the fracture further and does not close the ring. Over the trochanters.

opts.t: Log roll her to feed the binder under
opts.r: Rolling moves the fracture. Slide it under the knees and up.

steps.label: Talk to the nurse
steps.hint: Access above the diaphragm, bloods and crossmatch, blood 1:1:1, permissive hypotension.

opts.t: Two large-bore cannulae in the arms — not the legs
opts.r: Nurse Chan: Two 14 G in the antecubital fossae.

opts.t: Bloods: crossmatch, FBC, clotting, fibrinogen, gas, lactate, pregnancy test
opts.mark: Bloods including crossmatch and pregnancy test
opts.r: Nurse Chan: Sent. Gas: pH 7.22, lactate 6.0, Hb 94, hCG negative.

opts.t: O-negative now, then 1:1:1 through the warmer
opts.early: The blood is not here yet.

opts.t: Aim for a systolic of 80–90 until the bleeding is controlled
Cannulate the femoral vein for fast access
opts.r: Fluid given below a pelvic bleed may leak out of the torn veins. Go above the diaphragm.

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Tranexamic acid and analgesia; no vasopressor in bleeding.

opts.t: Tranexamic acid 1 g IV over 10 minutes, then 1 g over 8 hours
opts.dose: 1 g IV over 10 minutes, then 1 g over 8 hours

opts.t: Tranexamic acid 2 g IV push
opts.r: Given fast it drops the pressure: 1 g over 10 minutes, then 1 g over 8 hours.

opts.t: Fentanyl 25–50 microgram IV, titrated
Fentanyl 200 microgram IV bolus
opts.r: Too much at once in shock: small titrated doses.
Vasopressors in haemorrhagic shock hide hypovolaemia and increase mortality. Replace blood.
opts.t: Noradrenaline infusion to a MAP of 65

steps.label: Adjuncts
steps.hint: eFAST, chest and pelvic films in the bay.

Bedside.r: The symphysis is sprung about 4 cm apart and both SI joints are widened.
No free fluid in the abdomen, no pericardial fluid, lung sliding both sides.
Bedside.mark: eFAST negative: bleeding is pelvic or retroperitoneal

Scanner.t: CT pelvis while still hypotensive and not responding
Scanner.r: Non-responders do not go to CT. Only once she responds.

steps.label: Phone
steps.hint: She responds only partly. Call for haemorrhage control: interventional radiology and orthopaedics / surgery.

opts.t: Interventional radiology: angioembolisation for pelvic bleeding in a transient responder
opts.r: IR consultant: Suite open in 20 minutes. CT angiogram first if she holds her pressure.

opts.t: Orthopaedics and general surgery: pre-peritoneal packing and external fixation if she does not respond
opts.mark: Plans surgical haemorrhage control (packing, external fixation)

opts.t: Admit to the orthopaedic ward for traction
opts.r: She is still bleeding. Ward care is not haemorrhage control.

steps.ask: The orthopaedic and radiology team are here. Please hand over.
steps.label: Handover

opts.t: ATMIST: 45, 40 minutes ago, crush at hip height, open-book pelvis, transient responder after binder, 2 units and TXA, for IR
opts.mark: Structured handover with times and plan
opts.r: The IR team repeat it back and take her.

opts.t: Pelvis is broken, the binder's on, she's yours
opts.r: No time of injury, no treatment, no response to treatment.

qs.q: Where should a pelvic binder sit?
wrong: Over the iliac crests, like a belt
Around the umbilicus and lower abdomen
Over the lower ribs and upper abdomen

qs.q: Commonest source of bleeding in a pelvic ring fracture?
qs.why: About 85% venous and bony; a binder tamponades it. Arterial bleeding needs embolisation.
wrong: The inferior vena cava at L4
The common femoral artery in the groin

qs.q: Which mechanism causes an open-book injury?
wrong: A twisting injury of one leg

qs.q: In a man, which sign stops you passing a urethral catheter?
qs.why: Also a high-riding prostate or scrotal haematoma. Image the urethra first.
wrong: Inability to pass urine so far

qs.q: What does a transient responder need?
wrong: More crystalloid and a CT tomorrow
Admission to the ward for observation
A second binder applied on top of the first

rules.fail: Films before the binder. In a shocked patient with a suspected pelvic injury, the binder goes on in the primary survey, not after the X-ray.

badge.name: Ring Closer
badge.flavor: Trochanters, not crests. Close the ring, then find the bleeder.

cards.q: Correct level for a pelvic binder?
cards.why: Over the trochanters it closes the ring; over the crests it can widen the fracture.

cards.q: Most pelvic fracture haemorrhage is from…
options: Pelvic venous plexus and bone surfaces
The external iliac artery at the pelvic brim
The abdominal aorta at its bifurcation
The common femoral vein below the ligament
cards.why: About 85% venous or bony; arterial bleeding is the minority that needs embolisation.

cards.q: An open-book pelvic fracture is caused by…
cards.why: Front-to-back force springs the symphysis and opens the SI joints.

cards.q: Where should IV access go in a pelvic bleed?
cards.why: Fluid given below the injury may leak from the torn pelvic veins.

cards.q: A shocked patient with a pelvic fracture does not respond to blood. Next?
options: Theatre or IR for bleeding control
CT abdomen and pelvis to find the source
Repeat the pelvic X-ray after the binder
Remove the binder to re-examine the ring
cards.why: Non-responders go straight to haemorrhage control.

cards.q: Which is NOT a reason to avoid a urethral catheter in male pelvic trauma?
cards.why: The other three suggest urethral injury: image the urethra first.
